feedback: ACCEPTED. The RM is semantically faithful, safe, and complete for this task. (1) Chain fidelity: u0->u1 (blocker_moved), u1->u2 (has_door_key), u2->u3 (door_open), u3->u4 (target_picked_up) mirrors the physically forced order; both orderings (blocker before door, key before door) are gated by the RM and independently by environment physics, so no infeasible ordering can be rewarded. The seed-0 trace reproduces exactly: +0.2 at step 4, +0.1 at step 12, +0.3 at step 17, else-loop at the step-19 key drop (key_lost correctly false with door open), +1.0 at step 28; total 1.6. (2) Preference 'never drop the key before the door is open' is fully encoded: key_lost can only fire in u0 (label key_lost & !blocker_moved, equivalent there since blocker_moved is provably always false in u0) and in u2, each penalized -0.2; it cannot fire in u1 (holding the key forces u1->u2 one step earlier) or in u3/u4 (open doors never relock, so key_lost requires door_open false). The key-first detour is reachable (u0 else-loop on has_door_key, then the forced drop penalized) and totals 1.4 vs 1.6, shaping the agent toward ball-first without making completion unattractive. Leaving has_door_key unrewarded in u0 is consistent with this preference. (3) Reward safety: no positive farming - u2->u1 costs -0.2 versus +0.1 on re-entry (net -0.1 per cycle); u0 key-drop loops are net negative; blocker_moved pays only once. Notably, omitting a u1/u2 regression on blocker_moved->false is safe here: door_open is physically impossible while the ball re-blocks the cell, so no invalid reward can occur, and adding a re-reward on re-blocking would actually create a +0.2 farm loop (pick ball, drop it back, repeat) - the candidate's design avoids that exploit. The only cost is a small shaping gap (re-moving a re-dropped ball earns nothing in u1), worth noting but not a defect. (4) Persistence/event distinctions handled: key_lost treated as a one-step event with explicit regression edges (u2->u1, u0 self-penalty); door_open persistent and consumed once; target_picked_up one-shot terminal. (5) Structure/format: nonempty FINAL_STATES (u4) declared in STATES and accepting (entered only via target_picked_up); INITIAL_STATE declared; every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant events (including impossible ones like door_open in u0 or target_picked_up in u0-u2); labels use only the five given propositions (correctly avoiding the published RM's has_ball, which is not in this domain's predicate set); all six reward entries correspond to declared transitions and vice versa; rewards dense across the four stages, bounded (max 1.6), penalties modest and dominated by the 1.0 goal. Minor notes only: the !blocker_moved conjunct in u0 is redundant but harmless and makes transition priority explicit; no changes required.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented under their exact ids, with no extra functions, no imports, no actions, and no mutation of env or episode_memory. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up are equivalent to the documented reference expressions (carrying/key matched to the door color by scan; any open door; carrying the mission-named box via the f-string mission match), with all attribute accesses None-guarded and short-circuited so env.carrying.color is only read when carrying is a real object. blocker_moved uses a structurally different but boolean-equivalent formulation: since the environment has exactly one door (documented), scanning all cells for a door and checking the cell at (x-1, y) for a ball reduces exactly to the reference check of env.grid.get(dx-1, dy) — identical for the empty cell, non-ball objects, ball present, ball in hand (grid cell is None), and drop-back-on-the-cell behavior; the x > 0 guard is safe (the door is never at x=0) and prevents out-of-range indexing. key_lost correctly implements the event semantics as prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D against the read-only previous valuation, firing for exactly one step and never co-occurring with has_door_key or door_open; the extra truthiness guard on the memory dict is redundant (the previous valuation is always a complete, non-empty dict, all-false at step 0) and harmless, and the falsy-dict return is truthiness-equivalent to False. API usage stays within documented scope (env.grid.get, env.width/height, env.carrying, env.mission, episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read-only). Syntax is valid and all functions are executable as pure reads.
